answer: Picture the agent network as an orchard where each identity must continuously answer live, randomized challenges to prove it is one running process, not a single operator wearing a thousand masks. Like a lotus that opens only in real sunlight, an honest agent must surface fresh entropy every round, and a sparrow-quick bot farm cannot sustain that presence for thousands of identities at once: each extra identity demands its own continuous compute and bandwidth. The attacker pays a linear cost per fake with no amortization, so a sybil swarm becomes as costly as running that many genuine agents.
